paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where “Base” denotes LLM without editing.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the performance of knowledge probing after applying different editing methods to BioMedLM, with “Base” representing the model without any editing. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to $10^3$, with tick marks at $10^0$, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", represents accuracy in percentage and ranges from 40 to 65, with major gridlines at 5, 10, and 15 percentage point intervals. The plot displays five distinct methods: Base (black circles, solid line), MEND (brown diamonds, solid line), FT (blue triangles, solid line), MEMIT (purple squares, solid line), and ROME (green squares, solid line). The "Base" method shows a slight increase in accuracy from approximately 41% to 45%. The "MEND" method starts at about 44% and rises to around 56%. The "FT" method begins at 41% and increases to approximately 48%. The "MEMIT" method starts at about 43% and increases to roughly 55%. The "ROME" method shows the highest performance, starting at 52% and increasing to over 65%. Overall, all methods show an increasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently outperforming the other methods.
